payload.rationale: As of September 17, 2026, the US has recorded 3,471 measles cases. To exceed the 6,000 case threshold by the end of the year, the US would need over 2,530 additional cases in the remaining 3.5 months (about 15 weeks). This requires an average of roughly 168 cases per week, which is nearly double the year-to-date average of about 93 cases per week. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that measles outbreaks often peak in the late winter and spring, meaning the incidence rate might actually decline in the fall, making the 6,000 threshold even further out of reach. The strongest reason this estimate could be too low is that the start of the school year could fuel rapid transmission in under-vaccinated communities, and reporting lags could mean the true current case count is already significantly higher than 3,471.
limitations: Relies on provisional CDC data, which is subject to reporting lags and revisions.
Does not use a formal epidemiological model to project the trajectory of the 39 current outbreaks.
Assumes historical seasonal patterns of measles transmission hold true for 2026.
